explanation: His short-stemmed, disease-resistant wheat sharply raised harvests in Mexico and South Asia, part of the shift in farming known as the Green Revolution.

claims.text: Norman Borlaug bred high-yield, disease-resistant wheat varieties.
Norman Borlaug was awarded the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize, for his contribution to the green revolution.
Borlaug's prize-winning breeding work was on wheat, not on rice, maize or soya beans.
Borlaug's semi-dwarf, disease-resistant wheat varieties greatly increased harvests in Mexico and in South Asia, notably India and Pakistan.
This rise in crop yields is known as the Green Revolution.
